Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Chromatin accessibility memory after transient stimulus
ideas.description: Stimulate cells (e.g., with TPA, growth factor, or injury signal), then wash out and perform ATAC-seq and AP-1 (FOS/JUN) CUT&RUN at time points over days to weeks. Persistent AP-1 motif-containing accessible sites after AP-1 levels return to baseline would indicate a retained memory state. Like the material's string of random-looking characters, the sites that persist are a sparse signal that must be separated from noise by comparing against unstimulated controls and shuffled-motif backgrounds.

ideas.title: Acute degron depletion to separate initiation from maintenance
ideas.description: Use auxin-inducible degron tagging of FOS or JUN (or a dominant-negative A-FOS) to remove AP-1 either during the stimulus or only after memory is established. If accessibility and the enhanced secondary response persist after depletion post-establishment, AP-1 is needed only for writing the memory. If they collapse, AP-1 is needed for maintaining it.

ideas.title: Re-stimulation response assay (primed vs naive)
ideas.description: Give a first stimulus, rest the cells, then give a second stimulus. Compare RNA-seq and nascent transcription (PRO-seq) between primed and naive cells, and check whether the faster or stronger induction is limited to AP-1-bound loci. Include a no-first-stimulus control and a first-stimulus-with-AP-1-inhibition control to show the dependence.

ideas.title: Single-cell multiome lineage tracing of memory inheritance
ideas.description: Do single-cell RNA and ATAC profiling, with barcodes or live reporter imaging to identify sister cells, after a transient stimulus and several divisions. Test whether sister cells share AP-1 site accessibility and responsiveness more than random pairs, which would indicate mitotic inheritance. Live-cell AP-1 reporters can also show whether the memory is bistable or graded.

ideas.title: Sufficiency test by synthetic AP-1 perturbation and histone context
ideas.description: Use dCas9-based recruitment or an inducible pulse of AP-1 at a defined enhancer, and measure whether it creates lasting accessibility and H3K27ac/H3K4me1 after the trigger is removed. Pair this with perturbation of cofactors such as BAF/SWI-SNF, and with motif mutation by CRISPR base editing. This tests whether AP-1 alone is sufficient and which co-factors stabilize the memory.
